svg.title: Orbit Remote hardware streaming pipeline
svg.desc: The hardware streaming pipeline, on by default for Windows hosts, with per-stage measurements at 3024×1898: capture with DXGI Desktop Duplication on the GPU, 4.4 ms per changed frame and nothing for an unchanged screen; hardware H.264 encoding through Windows Media Foundation, 5.8 to 7.6 ms, or 2.5 to 2.9 ms at 1080p; sending one stream inside the pinned mutual-TLS link within WireGuard, 2 to 26 KB per update instead of about 1 MB; WebCodecs hardware decoding, 0.5 to 0.7 ms on Windows and 2.4 to 3.3 ms on an Apple-silicon Mac; and drawing to a canvas in 0.2 ms. The stage times add up to about 11 to 13 ms per frame plus the network; this sum is not a latency measurement. Measured live on one PC: 59.3 frames per second at native 2560 by 1440 on a real desktop with 0.6 ms decode and about 300 KB/s, against about 20 frames per second at 12.5 MB/s for images; a 60-second synthetic test drew 3601 of 3601 frames at 60.0 frames per second. Click-to-screen latency and video between two computers are not measured yet.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
